gaps.sentence: The report ___ have been finished yesterday; the deadline was missed.
gaps.explanation: 'Should have been finished' — it was expected but did not happen.

gaps.sentence: You ___ see a doctor about that cough; it has lasted three weeks.
gaps.explanation: 'Should' gives advice or a recommendation: should see.

gaps.sentence: Where is Anna? I am not sure — she ___ be in the library.
gaps.hint: an uncertain possibility, not really sure
gaps.explanation: 'Might' expresses a possibility the speaker is unsure about: might be.

gaps.sentence: You ___ better take an umbrella; it looks like rain.
She ___ have brought a present, but it was kind of her anyway.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't have' plus the participle means the action happened but was unnecessary: needn't have brought.

gaps.sentence: I do not know whose coat this is — it ___ belong to one of the guests.
gaps.explanation: 'Might' hedges a guess when the speaker is not sure: might belong.

gaps.sentence: This bill ___ be right — we only ordered two coffees.
gaps.hint: an obvious mistake, so it is impossible
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' shows the speaker believes something is not possible: can't be right.

gaps.sentence: You ___ worry — I have already sent the invitations.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' reassures someone that an action is unnecessary: needn't worry.
